title: 2024 against 2025: the apparent relationship lives in the thin per-season samples
claim: Per-player mean retention in 2024 against 2025: r = 0.1959 across all 66 players with a turn in both seasons, and r = 0.0067 across the 39 players with at least 10 turns in each. The apparent relationship lives in the thin per-season samples.

caveats: Measurement ceiling: 2,197 of 7,777 turns sit at exactly 1.000, pulling every player mean toward the same value.

Regression to the mean: both axes are per-season means and therefore noisy; splitting one player's turns by season enlarges that noise, which flattens the cloud even when a real player effect exists. Neither panel estimates a player effect.
DB only; no other position group is drawn, not even as context.
Exploratory: not one of the four report figures; written output does not cite it.
